summary.headline: ABCL Q2 FY27 consolidated PAT rose 38% YoY to ₹1,288 crore on revenue of ₹16,545 crore; NBFC ROA reached 2.45%.
summary.overview: Consolidated PAT was ₹1,288 crore, up 38% YoY and 10% QoQ, with revenue of ₹16,545 crore (up 31% YoY). NBFC PAT rose 41% YoY to ₹1,008 crore with ROA of 2.45% and credit cost of 0.92%, close to the 2.5% ROA target management had set for Q4. HFC PAT rose 73% YoY to ₹261 crore, with AUM up 50% YoY. Management flagged that the rate hikes will raise funding costs, with a further 5-10 bps expected in Q3, and that NBFC margins will expand only gradually as the mix shifts to unsecured lending. The call also covered life insurance and health insurance regulatory risk from the proposed EoM (commission) caps.

segments.name: NBFC (Retail, MSME, Corporate)
segments.commentary: AUM ₹1,76,557 crore (+26.5% YoY); MSME AUM ₹1,01,119 crore (57% of book, +30% YoY); Personal & Consumer AUM ₹24,955 crore (+37% YoY); corporate 29% of book, +15% YoY. Entity GS3 1.28%, PCR 48.4%.

segments.name: Housing Finance (ABHFL)
segments.commentary: AUM ₹57,373 crore (+50% YoY); disbursements ₹8,957 crore (+55% YoY); GS2+GS3 0.65% (-45 bps YoY), GS3 0.37%. Target ₹1 lakh crore+ AUM in 8-10 quarters and 15% ROE.

segments.name: Asset Management (ABSLAMC)
segments.commentary: Mutual fund quarterly average AUM ₹4.42 lakh crore (+4% YoY); equity MF AUM ₹2.09 lakh crore (+9% YoY); ETF AUM +42% YoY vs industry +27%; about 85% of funds in top quartile. Total average AUM ₹11.06 lakh crore including ESIC/EPFO mandates.

segments.name: Life Insurance (ABSLI)
segments.commentary: Individual APE/FYP +25% YoY in H1 vs industry 13%; H1 total premium ₹12,656 crore (+42%); AUM ₹1,20,736 crore (+16%); solvency 190%; opex to premium 21.2%.

segments.name: Health Insurance
segments.commentary: Gross premium H1 ₹4,543 crore (+48% YoY); retail +43%, corporate +55%; market share 14.2% vs 13.6%; H1 profit ₹46 crore under IFRS; combined ratio 107%.

guidance_outlook: NBFC ROA to be close to 2.5% by Q4 FY27; management says it is 'almost there' at 2.45% and intends to sustain it.
NBFC opex to AUM expected to stay in the 1.85%-1.9% range, including gold loan branch investments.
Cost of borrowing expected to rise another 5-10 bps in Q3 FY27 if rate trend continues; 57% of borrowings floating, 70% of loan book floating.
Life insurance: individual FYP CAGR of 20%+ for next 3 years, VNB margin above 20%, and net VNB to double in 3 years.
HFC: target ₹1 lakh crore+ AUM and 15% ROE over next 8-10 quarters.
Gold loans: 200-300 dedicated branches by March 2027, scaling to 1,000+ branches over 3 years.
capex_capacity: Gold loan business launched in August 2026: 70 branches opened in ~70 days, AUM ₹200 crore; phased rollout of 200-300 dedicated branches by March 2027.
HFC: more than 100 new branches launched so far in FY27, across metros, Tier 1 and Tier 2/3 markets.

Life insurance: plans to add people and branches in the proprietary channel this year; IndusInd Bank onboarded as bancassurance partner, business commencement targeted by Q4 FY27; 11 existing partner banks.
Health: proprietary agent base above 2.40 lakh agents, up 51% YoY.
demand_pricing: NBFC sourcing ₹24,708 crore in Q2, near the record set in Q4 FY26; retail and MSME were 71% of H1 disbursements vs 67% a year earlier.
NBFC Q2 disbursements: Personal & Consumer ₹5,877 crore (+18% YoY); Secured MSME +22% YoY; unsecured business loans ₹1,515 crore (+9% QoQ), with new products ~28% of sourcing.
NBFC lending rates raised by 25 bps effective 26 October on variable-rate book (~70% of loans); HFC PLR raised by 20 bps effective 1 November.
HFC: management says BT-outs run at about 5-5.5% with BT-ins about 2x that; competitors (Bajaj, Tata) have also raised rates.
Life insurance: 98% of net VNB from individual business; ULIP share 34%, traditional incl. protection 66%; annuity 14% of retail new business; group life growth 90%.
Management says it is not in a hurry to add high-risk customers to lift margins; NBFC margin expansion expected over a few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NBFC retail disbursement growth QoQ moderate to about 12% vs the usual 20-30%, and was there pricing screening?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied any slowdown and said growth is calibrated to risk-reward and cycles. Personal & Consumer AUM grew 37% YoY and unsecured business 53% YoY; supply-chain utilisation and repayments cause quarterly swings.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NBFC employee opex fall QoQ despite branch additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 had a one-off; costs normalised in Q2. Opex/AUM is expected to stay at 1.85%-1.9% even with gold loan branch investment.

qa_highlights.question: Why did HFC cost of funds rise, and was PLR raised?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of funds rose 11 bps (6.00% to 6.11%), partly from higher leverage after the April capital infusion; cost of borrowing 7.46% to 7.47%. PLR raised 20 bps effective 1 November.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to drought-hit agri segments, and how will EoM caps affect life and health insurers?
qa_highlights.answer: NBFC has no direct agri exposure; inflation impact is being monitored. In life, management says the opex-to-premium ratio is 21.2%, direct business is 8-9% of the mix (from 2-3%), and the regulation will bring bank-branch access benefits. Health says it wants no arbitrage between monoline and multiline players.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook and when does the unsecured mix show up in margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Unsecured mix rose about 1% QoQ, but the benefit was offset by higher cost of funds, so margin did not expand. Management expects margin expansion over a few quarters and is prioritising risk-adjusted return over margin.

qa_highlights.question: What levers drive ROA beyond credit cost below 1%, and will disbursement yields feed into book yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Levers are margin, opex, credit cost and product mix. Disbursement yields are much higher than book yield, but this will take time on a ₹1.8 lakh crore book. New unsecured lending is ROA-accretive.

qa_highlights.question: After the rate hike, what is the cost of funds on book vs incremental basis, and should a management overlay be applied?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental cost rose 11 bps QoQ; Q3 expects 5-10 bps more. Borrowings are 57% floating and loans 70% floating, so repricing offsets this. A management overlay was created for stressed segments since the Iran-US conflict began and sits within the reported credit cost.

risks_watch: Funding cost pressure: incremental cost of borrowing up 11 bps QoQ, with 5-10 bps more expected in Q3 FY27; margin expansion depends on repricing.
Macro stress: drought declared in six states, higher inflation, and the Iran-US conflict; management says it uses an overlay in credit cost but has not quantified it.
Life and health insurance: proposed EoM (commission) caps could cut the opex/premium ratio from ~21.2%; regulation still at consultation stage.
Retail unsecured growth (Personal & Consumer +37% YoY) carries inflation and credit risk; management says it is calibrating risk.
Gold loan rollout: 200-300 branches by March 2027, a new product whose scale-up and asset quality are still unproven (AUM ₹200 crore).
key_quotes: We already are almost there at 2.45% ROA in quarter 2.
So, whatever fits our risk profile and is within our risk appetite is what we are looking at building the portfolio. But it will happen. I think a few more quarters is what we are looking at.
We created some management overlay, but that's part of the overall credit cost, which you see here.
No. We are looking at this segment in a very calibrated manner, which fits our risk reward and our risk appetite.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on headline NBFC ROA (2.45%, "almost there" vs 2.5% Q4 target) and asset quality, but cautious and somewhat evasive on margin expansion timing, the EoM commission-cap impact on life and health insurance, and quantification of macro overlays. Answers on the retail disbursement slowdown and the cost-of-funds question were defensive, with management denying any slowdown and stressing risk calibration.

adds.what: Gold loan dedicated branches: 200-300 by March 2027, scaling to 1,000+ over 3 years (70 opened in ~70 days so far)
HFC: more than 100 new branches launched in FY27 across metros, Tier 1 and Tier 2/3
Life insurance: IndusInd Bank bancassurance partner, business commencement targeted by Q4 FY27

growth.why: Guidance is for NBFC ROA near 2.5% by Q4 FY27 (currently 2.45%), life individual FYP CAGR 20%+ for 3 years, HFC AUM ₹1 lakh crore+ in 8-10 quarters, backed by 100+ HFC branches, 70 gold loan branches and a phased 200-300 gold branch rollout by March 2027, with partial specifics on orders and sourcing (₹24,708 crore NBFC Q2 sourcing).

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NBFC margin expansion expected only gradually over a few quarters as unsecured mix rises, but cost of borrowing rises another 5-10 bps in Q3 FY27 and margin did not expand QoQ in Q2; NBFC ROA 2.45% vs 2.5% Q4 target.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 70 gold loan branches already opened in ~70 days with a phased plan of 200-300 by March 2027, and 100+ HFC branches launched in FY27 (commissioned).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: NBFC AUM +26.5% YoY to ₹1,76,557 crore, Q2 sourcing ₹24,708 crore near record, HFC AUM +50% YoY and life individual APE +25% vs industry 13%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; the call covers branch rollouts rather than plant or capital expenditure.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided NBFC ROA only to 'closer to 2.5%' by Q4 FY27 and kept opex/AUM at 1.85%-1.9%, so no raise is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Cost of borrowing set to rise another 5-10 bps in Q3 FY27, with macro stress (drought in six states, Iran-US conflict) and an unquantified overlay; EoM caps could hit life and health opex economics.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Gold loan dedicated branches scaling to 200-300 by March 2027, and IndusInd Bank bancassurance business targeted to commence by Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Life insurance individual FYP CAGR 20%+ for 3 years
rows.why: Individual APE/FYP grew 25% YoY in H1 vs industry 13%, and management guided a 20%+ CAGR with VNB margin above 20% (H1 FY27 at 16.1%).

rows.label: HFC AUM ₹1 lakh crore+ and 15% ROE
rows.why: HFC AUM is ₹57,373 crore (+50% YoY) with ROE at 11.47% and disbursements +55% YoY, so the target needs continued growth at this pace.

rows.label: EoM commission caps on life and health insurers
rows.why: Opex-to-premium in life is 21.2%, and health combined ratio is 107%, so caps could pressure insurer economics, though regulation is still at consultation stage.

tone.note: Management was confident on NBFC ROA (2.45%, 'almost there' vs 2.5% Q4 target) and asset quality, but cautious and evasive on margin timing, EoM cap impact on insurers and macro overlay quantification; analysts pressed on the QoQ disbursement slowdown and cost of funds.
